relationships.title: Nvidia equity in SB Energy (prepaid forward and IPO private placement)
relationships.insight_template: Nvidia paid {funded} for {counterparty} shares and would owe {contingent_max} more only if the listing closes in time, beside its lease guarantee.
relationships.definition: Nvidia prepaid $1.5 billion to SB Energy's parent on 17 August 2026 under a prepaid forward contract that settles into non voting Class N shares at 90% of the IPO price; this is the committed and funded amount. It also signed a share purchase agreement to buy another $1.5 billion of Class N shares at the IPO price, which lapses unless an IPO with at least $1.5 billion of primary proceeds closes by 15 May 2027, so that part is recorded as contingent. Nvidia's own release mentioned only $1.5 billion.

committed_total.note: The prepaid forward already funded on 17 August 2026. The second $1.5 billion lapses unless the IPO closes in time, so it sits in contingent_max.

components.note: Nvidia funded the full prepaid forward on 2026-08-17 (S-1/A, ev_40087).

contingent_max.trigger: SB Energy completes an IPO generating at least $1.5 billion of primary gross proceeds (ev_100052); the share purchase agreement terminates automatically on 15 May 2027 if the private placement has not closed (ev_100023)
contingent_max.note: Concurrent private placement of Class N shares at the IPO price under the share purchase agreement dated 17 August 2026.

reconciliation.nvidia_side: Nvidia's 8-K press release says it will invest $1.5 billion in SB Energy (ev_30010, 2026-08-17). No later Nvidia disclosure of the prepaid forward or the second $1.5 billion found as of 2026-11-23.
reconciliation.counterparty_side: SB Energy's S-1/A No. 3 says Nvidia will invest $3.0 billion in total (ev_40086): $1.5 billion funded on 17 August 2026 under the prepaid forward (ev_40087) and $1.5 billion committed in a private placement at the IPO price (ev_40088), which lapses on 15 May 2027 if not closed (ev_100023) and needs an IPO with at least $1.5 billion of primary proceeds (ev_100052).

differences.counterparty_value: $3.0 billion ($1.5 billion prepaid forward funded plus $1.5 billion IPO private placement)
Prepaid forward settles at 90% of IPO price, worth about $1.667 billion at the IPO price; placement at the IPO price

credit.wwr_reason: Equity value moves with AI data center demand. Correlation with the Nvidia residual value guaranty on the same campus is high: an OpenAI default would both trigger the guaranty and cut SB Energy's main future revenue (analysis).
credit.collateral: None. Before the IPO Nvidia holds a contract claim on Energy Global and SB Energy under the prepaid forward; after settlement it holds non voting Class N common stock, structurally junior to all project debt.
credit.tenor: Prepaid forward has no stated maturity and settles on an IPO, listing, financing, change of control or dissolution; share purchase agreement lapses 15 May 2027.
credit.notes: SB Energy records the prepaid forward as a liability at $1,666,667 thousand fair value at 30 Sept 2026 (ev_100053).

first_order.trigger: SB Energy's IPO does not close by 15 May 2027
first_order.mechanism: The share purchase agreement lapses and the prepaid forward settles under its non IPO terms
first_order.text: If the SB Energy IPO fails, Nvidia's second $1.5 billion is never paid but its funded $1.5 billion stays in an unlisted SoftBank controlled company.

first_order.mechanism: SB Energy carries construction costs without lease revenue, lowering the value of the Class N shares
first_order.text: A delay at PORTS-Pike, SB Energy's largest asset, would cut the value of Nvidia's shares at the same time as it delays Nvidia's guaranty taking effect.

second_order.trigger: Nvidia becomes a shareholder at the IPO
second_order.mechanism: Investors see the supplier and guarantor of the campus also buying stock at or below the IPO price
second_order.text: Nvidia buying SB Energy stock at 90% of the IPO price lends support to the offering, which a withdrawal by Nvidia would remove (analysis).

second_order.mechanism: SB Energy loses most of its contracted data center revenue while Nvidia's guaranty and equity are hit together
second_order.text: Because SB Energy has no unaffiliated data center tenants, an OpenAI failure would hit SB Energy, its lenders and Nvidia's stake at once.

second_order.mechanism: The campus must use Nvidia reference architecture for twenty years, so Nvidia money supports future demand for its own systems
second_order.text: Nvidia cash in SB Energy funds a campus that must exclusively deploy Nvidia hardware, so part of future Nvidia sales rests on Nvidia's own capital.

relationships.title: Residual value support for AI compute financing platforms (MOUs with six capital providers)
relationships.insight_template: Nvidia may back part of the value of projects that the {counterparty} fund, so a fall in asset values could become its loss.
relationships.definition: In August 2026 Nvidia signed memorandums of understanding with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to set up platforms that would raise over $500 billion of third party capital for AI infrastructure. Nvidia says it may provide residual value support for up to 25% of an opportunity, at its option and project by project. The arrangements are preliminary and subject to final agreements.

reconciliation.nvidia_side: Nvidia press release (ev_30014, ev_30015, ev_30016), blog (ev_30013) and 10-Q MD&A (ev_10045, ev_10046, ev_100006) describe MOUs, preliminary, with optional residual value support.
reconciliation.counterparty_side: No disclosure found as of 2026-11-23 in SEC filings of Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs or KKR (EDGAR full text searches for NVIDIA with memorandum, financing platform and residual value). The only counterparty voice is a KKR executive quote inside the Nvidia release (ev_30017).

credit.wwr_reason: Residual value support pays when the value of financed AI assets falls, which is when platform borrowers and Nvidia demand are both weak.
credit.collateral: Not defined; would be the financed projects.
credit.notes: Type RV rather than GU: Nvidia's own words are residual value support for a portion of specific projects (ev_10046, ev_30013), not a guarantee of a named obligation. The $500 billion is third party capital, not Nvidia's, so it is not entered as headline. Up to 25% is a share per opportunity, not an amount.

first_order.trigger: A project financed by a platform with Nvidia residual value support loses value
first_order.mechanism: Nvidia pays the shortfall on up to its share of the opportunity under the six financing platforms memorandums
first_order.text: If a project financed by one of the six platforms with Nvidia residual value support loses value, Nvidia would cover the shortfall on up to a quarter of that opportunity, but no support is in place until final agreements are signed.

second_order.trigger: Capital providers size platform debt against Nvidia support
second_order.mechanism: Lenders in the six financing platforms could price loans on Nvidia's support once final agreements exist
second_order.text: Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR could price platform loans on Nvidia's residual value support, but the partnerships still await final agreements, so no lender can rely on it yet.

second_order.trigger: Nvidia supports values of GPU heavy projects
second_order.mechanism: Support under the six financing platforms would prop up the collateral value of Nvidia systems used in other financings
second_order.text: If Nvidia gives residual value support on projects of the six platforms, it would hold up GPU collateral values that other lenders also rely on (analysis).

The offering is Meta's own Class A common stock, sold through forward sale agreements, with a concurrent mandatory convertible preferred offering. Meta's prospectus names Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom as cornerstone investors who indicated interest in up to $5.0 billion in total, and says the indications are not binding.

reconciliation.counterparty_side: Meta's final prospectus supplement: Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom indicated interest in up to $5.0 billion in aggregate (ev_100039, ev_100040), and these indications are not binding agreements or commitments to purchase (ev_100041). No Meta disclosure of shares actually sold to Nvidia found as of 2026-11-23.

relationships.title: Microsoft: co-investor with Nvidia in Anthropic and Anthropic's compute seller
relationships.insight_template: {counterparty} invests beside Nvidia in Anthropic and sells it cloud compute, so an Anthropic funding gap would hit both.
relationships.definition: Microsoft committed to invest up to $5 billion in Anthropic alongside Nvidia's up to $10 billion, and Anthropic committed to buy $30 billion of Azure compute. Microsoft has no Nvidia capital, guarantee or financing. It matters for the S2 lab funding gap scenario.
relationships.notes: Announced 18 November 2025 in a joint Nvidia, Microsoft and Anthropic release. Microsoft's purchases of neocloud capacity (Nebius, Nscale, IREN) are recorded by the neocloud colleagues.

relationships.title: Google: backstop of Fluidstack leases at TeraWulf (comparator)
relationships.insight_template: {counterparty} backs Fluidstack leases much as Nvidia backs OpenAI leases, so supplier credit support is not unique to Nvidia.
relationships.definition: In August 2025 Google agreed to backstop certain obligations of Fluidstack under its data center leases with TeraWulf, effective at lease commencement, in exchange for TeraWulf warrants. It is a comparator to Nvidia's lease guarantees and involves no Nvidia capital.
relationships.notes: TeraWulf 8-K of 14 August 2025. Cipher Mining reports a similar Google backstop (not extracted).

projects.name: PORTS-Pike Technology Campus, Buildings 1 to 9 (Nvidia guaranteed)
projects.location: Piketon, Pike County, Ohio, US (former DOE Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant site)
projects.gpu_generation: Nvidia DSX AI factory platform; generation not specified (each generation about 1.5 million GPUs per Nvidia, ev_30028)
projects.anchor_tenant: VELA I Holdings, LLC (OpenAI affiliate); OpenAI Global, LLC guarantees the tenant
projects.expected_completion: First building ready for service expected 2028 (Nvidia fiscal 2029); leases commence in stages 2028 to 2032
projects.notes: Nine leases (PORTS Building 1 to 9, LLC as landlords) each about 472 MW-IT (ev_100016), covered by nine residual value guaranties capped at $105 billion in total, about $24.7 billion per GW-IT (ev_100051, ev_100013). No project debt in place: construction pending local approval and financing (ev_100020); SB Energy targets up to 90% debt of $8 to $9 billion capex per building (ev_100019, ev_100018). Interconnection credit support could exceed $6 billion (ev_100022). AEP Ohio grid capex about $5.1 billion (ev_100021). Leases not commenced at 30 Sept 2026 (ev_100015).

projects.name: PORTS-Pike Technology Campus, Buildings 10 to 17 (Nvidia option)
projects.gpu_generation: Nvidia reference architecture required only where guaranteed; not specified
projects.notes: Eight leases with floating yield rent. Nvidia may, at its sole discretion, guarantee these buildings; if it does not by a date certain OpenAI must provide an A- rated replacement guarantor (ev_100025), and certain leases give SB Energy termination rights if credit support is not provided. Campus total 17 buildings, about 8.0 GW-IT (ev_100029), about 10 GW gross load (ev_100017).

events.summary: Nvidia signs the SB Energy prepaid forward and share purchase agreement and funds $1.5 billion, the same day as the PORTS-Pike guaranties.
Nvidia announces MOUs with six capital providers for AI compute financing platforms.
KKR launches Helix with Nvidia, KIA and Vistra as founding investors.
Brookfield launches its AI infrastructure program and fund with commitments including Nvidia.
Nvidia says it will invest $3 billion in Meta's equity offering.
Meta's final prospectus supplement calls the cornerstone indications of interest not binding.
Microsoft and Nvidia commit to invest in Anthropic, which commits to buy Azure compute.
Google agrees to backstop Fluidstack lease obligations at TeraWulf.
